weakness: The program only ever approached the press point along a short straight corridor from the front (small yaw and pitch variants). With a movable box standing in front of the switch, every pre-press pose was in collision or unreachable, so it gave up after trying both arms (8 of 10 seeds). It never looked at what else stood between the hand and the target.
how_found: Listing assumptions, the straight free corridor in front of the press point (A4) was the one a real robot meets most often: objects are routinely left in front of switches and buttons. The planner already avoided known obstacles in transit, so I suspected the failure would come at the final approach, which has to come straight on.
why_missed: In every training scene the switch stood alone on the table, so approach failures came only from reach limits. I treated an unreachable approach as a reachability problem (try another arm or angle), not as a sign that the scene must be changed first.
fix: Before pressing, the program lists every detected object, other than the target, whose box overlaps the corridor in front of the press point. It grasps each one and sets it down to the side. If the grasp is impossible (on one switch model the object is only 1 cm from the switch, and wider than the gripper's opening), it sweeps the object sideways with the closed gripper pointing down. The sweep is lowered next to the object with contact allowed, tried with the hand both ways round about its pointing axis (one side of the wrist sticks out and collides), and counts even when the reach ends early, because the corridor is re-checked afterwards. Three repair iterations: 0.8 (grasp and set aside), 0.7 (sweep added, still refused near the switch), 1.0 (sweep start widened, contact allowed on the descent, both hand orientations).
general_rule: Before any contact motion, check the whole approach corridor for other objects and clear the movable ones first, grasping them or, when no grasp fits, pushing them aside along a path the arm can actually reach, and then re-check that the corridor is clear rather than assuming the clearing motion finished.

weakness: The program judged 'done' from one ambiguous signal: the rocker stopped turning between two small push stages. With a stiff rocker it stops turning for several other reasons: the fingertip slid off it, the arm was not pushing hard enough, the finger face was hitting the plate, or the planner refused the next stage. Each of these was read as 'at the stop'. Also, its small, position-controlled stages produced too little force, and its tilted pushes moved along the hand's axis and slid off.
how_found: The stop test (A5) rested on the mechanism being easy to move: a stall could only mean the end of travel. Real switches and buttons are often stiff, so I raised the joint's friction. Screening showed partial turns on 7 of 10 seeds. In-process traces of the fingertip depth, against the commanded depth and the true joint angle, then separated the failure modes.
why_missed: On the easy mechanism every stall happened at the true stop, so the single test was always right. I never asked what else a stall could mean, nor that a position-controlled arm applies force only through how far it is held back from its target.
fix: Five repair iterations. (1) A stall counts only if the fingertip is held back from its commanded depth: a fingertip that runs on freely has slipped off (0.4). (2) Push along the direction the mechanism gives way (horizontal), whatever the hand's tilt, and judge a stall only after this push has turned the rocker (0.6). (3) When held back without turning, command deeper targets: a larger position error pushes harder; the stop is accepted only when held back firmly (2.5 cm) (0.7). (4) Level approaches turned about the vertical come before tilted ones (a level finger face meets the rocker before the plate), and a stop is accepted only after a second, independent push from another approach finds no more travel (0.7, now out of time). (5) Cheaper presses (6 coarser stages, a shorter pre-press distance, likely approaches first) to fit the time budget (0.8; all scenes base 1.0 / v1 1.0 / v2 0.9).
general_rule: Never read 'it stopped moving' as 'it is done' from one push: tell apart the possible causes (end of travel, too little force, slipping off, being blocked elsewhere) by checking how far the tool was held back from its commanded target, push harder by commanding a deeper target when resistance is the cause, and confirm completion with a second, independent attempt that finds no further travel.

weakness: The program measured the target once, before moving the arm, and aimed every later push at that spot. When the switch slid 8 cm sideways while the arm was on its way, every push hit the empty air or the plate edge beside it (0 of 10).
how_found: A1 (the target stays where it was measured) was the remaining assumption with a direct line of code relying on it: the single detection at the start. Screening showed that sideways and backwards slides broke it (0.0 and 0.1), while reorienting or moving the switch before the start did not.
why_missed: In every earlier scene the target was fixed for the whole episode, and the only re-measurements were of the rocker angle, which was itself the progress signal. The target's position was never treated as something that can go stale.
fix: One repair. Before every press attempt the program locates the press point again. It takes two averaged looks 0.3 s apart and accepts the position only when they agree within 1.2 cm (the target is still). If the target moved since the last look, the next attempt aims at the new position and push direction. Scenes: base 1.0, v1 0.9, v2 0.9, v3 1.0.
general_rule: Treat every target measurement as stale once the arm has moved: re-measure right before each contact attempt, accept the measurement only after two looks a moment apart agree (the target is still), and re-aim the attempt if it moved.
notes: oracle not meaningful for object_motion: RoboTwin's expert steps the scene itself, so scripted motions never run during its episode

weakness: The corridor-clearing step trusted the grasp's success flag. On a 5 kg blocker the grasp closed (both fingers on the box), but the hand could not carry it, so place() failed. The step then reported 'not cleared' and returned without trying the sideways sweep that would have worked. Where the grasp did not close, the sweep ran and the press succeeded, but only after a slow failed carry attempt ate most of the budget.
how_found: The round-1 repair added a new assumption: whatever blocks the corridor can be moved by grasping or sweeping it. A heavy object in the way is common on a real bench, so I made v1's blocker 5 kg. An in-process trace with the box's true position showed the sweep does move it, while eval traces ended early with the box untouched after a 'successful' grasp.
why_missed: In round 1 every grasp that closed could also lift the object, so 'grasped' and 'movable' were the same thing, and the fallback chain was written to run only when the grasp itself failed.
fix: One repair. After grasping a blocker, lift it 3 cm and check that its detected height rose. If not, it is too heavy to carry: release, retreat, and sweep it instead. After every clearing attempt (carry or sweep, either side), re-check the corridor and continue with the next method until it is clear. Scenes: base 0.9, v1 1.0, v2 0.9, v3 1.0, v4 0.9.
general_rule: Do not take an action's success flag as its effect: after grasping something you intend to move, test that it actually moves with the hand before committing to the move, and when a method fails, fall through to the next method instead of ending the attempt.
notes: related to round 1 (corridor clearing), but the failure is a different one: a false success from grasp that skipped the fallback

weakness: The approach corridor was checked once, at the start. A box that slid into it 1.5 s later (after the check, before the first press) blocked every pre-press pose, and the program gave up after trying every approach with both arms (0 of 10).
how_found: The round-1 repair checks the corridor once; A9 (nothing enters the push path later) was still unattacked. Objects being put down in front of a target is common around people. Screening showed an arrival at 1.5 s broke it fully (0.0) and at 3 s nearly so (0.2), while an arrival during the press did not (0.9).
why_missed: After round 3 I re-measured the target before every attempt, but I still treated the rest of the scene as fixed once checked. The obstacles were measured once like the target used to be.
fix: One repair. Before every press attempt, check the corridor again and clear anything that has entered it (the same grasp / lift-test / sweep step as at the start), re-close the pressing hand if clearing used it, then re-locate the switch. Scenes: base 1.0, v1 1.0, v2 0.9, v3 1.0, v4 1.0, v5 1.0.
general_rule: Re-check the whole relevant scene, not only the target, right before each attempt: anything measured before the arm moved, obstacles included, may have changed.
notes: round 3's rule (treat every measurement as stale once the arm has moved) already covers this when applied to obstacles; oracle not meaningful for object_motion (ISSUES 18)
